title: Multi-model assessment of nitracline depth and its basin structure

method.definition: depth of the maximum vertical nitrate gradient, taken across each layer's own bounds, searched within the top 1000 m
method.order_of_operations: the 1971-2000 climatological profile is formed first and the nitracline taken from it, because WOA23 nitrate exists only as a single all-period annual climatology at these depths
method.units: no conversion is needed for the depth: the maximum-gradient depth is invariant under scaling of the profile, verified as identical at every valid cell
method.climatology_periods: models 1971-2000, WOA23 nitrate 1965-2022 - a genuine mismatch that cannot be removed
method.grid: every reported number on the source's native grid with its own cell areas; regridding only for the pattern metrics of step 4 and for display
method.marginal_seas: folded into their parent ocean (select_basin default)
method.southern_and_arctic_oceans: separate basins in the WOA23 mask, not included in the Atlantic, Indian or Pacific numbers

basin_definitions.Pacific: WOA23 basinmask_01: Pacific Ocean, WOA23 codes [2, 12, 14, 18, 19, 25, 27, 28, 29, 33, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 44, 51, 54, 57, 59], with its marginal seas and sub-basins folded in (Sea of Japan, Sulu Sea, Sea of Okhotsk, Banda Sea, South China Sea, Celebes Sea, Aleutian Basin, Fiji Basin, Coral Sea, Southeast Pacific Basin, Guatemala Basin, East Caroline Basin, Marianas Basin, Philippine Sea, Chile Basin, Tasman Sea, Sulu Sea II, Java Sea, Chiloe); the Southern Ocean (WOA23 code 10) and the Arctic Ocean (code 11) are separate basins and are NOT included; the surface basin labels, applied through the whole water column
basin_definitions.Atlantic: WOA23 basinmask_01: Atlantic Ocean, WOA23 codes [1, 4, 5, 6, 9, 15, 16, 17, 20, 22, 23, 30, 31, 36, 37, 48, 49, 50, 55], with its marginal seas and sub-basins folded in (Mediterranean Sea, Baltic Sea, Black Sea, Hudson Bay, Baffin Bay, East Mediterranean, West Mediterranean, Caribbean Sea, North Caribbean, Gulf of Mexico, North American Basin, West European Basin, Southwest Atlantic Basin, Southeast Atlantic Basin, Guinea Basin, Brazil Basin, Argentine Basin, Venezuela Basin); the Southern Ocean (WOA23 code 10) and the Arctic Ocean (code 11) are separate basins and are NOT included; the surface basin labels, applied through the whole water column
basin_definitions.Indian: WOA23 basinmask_01: Indian Ocean, WOA23 codes [3, 7, 8, 21, 32, 34, 35, 43, 45, 46, 47, 56], with its marginal seas and sub-basins folded in (Red Sea, Persian Gulf, Andaman Basin, Southeast Indian Basin, East Indian Basin, Central Indian Basin, Arabian Sea, Somali Basin, Mascarene Basin, Crozet Basin, Bay of Bengal); the Southern Ocean (WOA23 code 10) and the Arctic Ocean (code 11) are separate basins and are NOT included; the surface basin labels, applied through the whole water column

findings: All three models place the nitracline too shallow globally, by 18 to 32 m, and the shortfall is worst in the Atlantic, where they are 53 to 74 m too shallow.
Only MPI-ESM1-2-LR reproduces the observed ordering of the three basins (Atlantic < Indian < Pacific); CESM2 and GFDL-ESM4 both put the Indian Ocean deepest.

Spatial correlations are low (0.40 to 0.60) and the RMSE is 152 to 163 m, far worse than a temperature-based diagnostic would give. Part of that is the diagnostic itself: where the profile is smooth the depth of the maximum gradient jumps between levels, and WOA23 has 47 levels in the top 1000 m against the models' 19 to 40, so the observed map is the patchiest of the four.

The equatorial Pacific section exposes a large CESM2 bias that the depth diagnostic alone does not show: below about 300 m in the eastern basin CESM2's nitrate falls to roughly a fifth of the observed value (8.5 against 40.2 micromoles per kilogram at 787 m, 110W), the signature of excessive water-column denitrification in an over-extended eastern tropical Pacific oxygen minimum zone. GFDL-ESM4 and MPI-ESM1-2-LR do not show it.
depends_on_tool_fix: layer_bounds_like in src/tools/data_loader.py now widens its level lookup by a 1e-4 m tolerance. CESM2 stores depth as float32 while the level table is float64, so before the fix every depth-range subset of CESM2 lost its deepest level and the vertical gradient could not be taken.
